name: s5_scorecards
title: The prediction rules do not beat 'always predict low' on the primary scorecard
caption: Each row is a pre-registered rule; dots show the share of rows it predicted correctly (colour = reader) and open diamonds the share an always-'low' predictor gets on the same cells; numbers at right are hits/rows. Bold rows aggregate the cells with Wilson 95% intervals (top: rules, bottom: baseline); dashed line is the declared 0.80 bar. All-low ties the rules on exp 22's primary scorecard (30/38 vs 30/38) and beats them on exp 19's (33/38 vs 31/38); the rules' margin comes from complement naming and the prompted cells, while 'NLA states exactly when statement-sayable' predicted low on every natural row and so equals the baseline. 'Complement (multi-choice)' is the pre-registered cell 'NLA names the complement': a multi-candidate forced-choice argmax on the unmarked value (prereg section 3), not a regex or judge verdict.
